blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary hospital antibiotic stewardship
stem: A hospital is revising its antibiotic stewardship program. Which proposed program design best reflects current CDC guidance?

options.A: Appoint an accountable leader or co-leaders, such as a physician and pharmacist, include pharmacy expertise, and implement active stewardship interventions.
options.B: Appoint a physician leader while pharmacists focus on dispensing and formulary logistics, with antimicrobial selection left to individual prescribers.
options.C: Assign pharmacists to review antibiotic utilization after treatment courses are completed, while active prescribing changes remain outside the stewardship program.
options.D: Place antibiotic-approval decisions with nursing and infection-prevention leaders, using physician or pharmacist review when a prescribing concern is referred.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's current Hospital Core Elements call for an accountable leader or co-leaders, such as a physician and pharmacist, responsible for stewardship program management and outcomes; CDC also identifies pharmacy expertise as a core element and recommends active interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization. B is incorrect because it restricts pharmacy participation to dispensing and logistics rather than stewardship expertise and antimicrobial-use improvement. C is incorrect because CDC stewardship action includes interventions that influence active antibiotic use, not merely retrospective utilization review after therapy is completed. D is incorrect because nursing and infection-prevention personnel can contribute to stewardship, but the cited CDC accountability and pharmacy-expertise elements support accountable physician/pharmacist leadership or involvement rather than shifting antibiotic-approval responsibility away from that expertise.
educational_objective: Recognize hospital antibiotic stewardship as a multidisciplinary management function that includes accountable leadership, meaningful pharmacy expertise, and active interventions to improve antibiotic use.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); SHEA/SIDP/PIDS/IDSA
source_document_title: Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs; Priorities for Hospital Core Element Implementation; Guidance for the Knowledge and Skills Required for Antimicrobial Stewardship Leaders
source_version_date: CDC Hospital Core Elements page dated September 15, 2025; CDC implementation priorities current page accessed 2026-08-20; multi-society guidance published May 11, 2026
source_locator: CDC Hospital Core Elements — Accountability: appoint a leader or co-leaders, such as a physician and pharmacist, responsible for program management and outcomes. Pharmacy Expertise: engage pharmacy expertise in stewardship. Action: implement interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization to improve antibiotic use. CDC Priorities — Accountability/Pharmacy-Stewardship Expertise/Action: physician-pharmacist co-leadership is an effective model; stewardship leaders should have appropriate training; prospective audit/feedback and preauthorization are priority interventions. 2026 SHEA/SIDP/PIDS/IDSA Guidance — Introduction: stewardship requires multidisciplinary clinical, pharmacology, microbiology, quality-improvement, communication, and program-evaluation expertise.
source_claim_supported: Current hospital stewardship guidance supports accountable leadership, meaningful pharmacist participation and expertise, and active prescribing-focused interventions rather than a dispensing-only or retrospective-only pharmacy role.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7/PDF page 11: 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care'; 'Participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes'; 'Utilize resources to promote quality client care.'
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7/PDF page 11 visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; no CACHE MISS.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'antimicrobial stewardship physician pharmacist prospective audit preauthorization' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Rebuilt all distractors to remove the 'only' cue and the uniquely long key. The revised alternatives test plausible stewardship-structure misconceptions: dispensing-only pharmacy involvement, retrospective-only review, and misassigned prescribing authority. Adversarial reread further separated CDC's Pharmacy Expertise and Action elements to avoid implying that pharmacy personnel must personally perform every active intervention.

option_audit.A: Correct; separately and accurately reflects CDC Accountability, Pharmacy Expertise, and Action elements without claiming physician-pharmacist co-leadership is the only acceptable structure.
option_audit.B: Plausible traditional-role misconception; incorrect because it strips pharmacists of the stewardship expertise CDC explicitly promotes.
option_audit.C: Plausible retrospective-quality-review misconception; incorrect because CDC recommends active stewardship interventions that can affect current prescribing.
option_audit.D: Plausible multidisciplinary-role misconception; incorrect because it shifts antibiotic-approval authority away from the accountable physician/pharmacist expertise described by CDC.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All options contain comparable organizational detail; the correct answer is not uniquely conspicuous by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel program-design statements within the same stewardship construct.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after source-based review. B and C underuse pharmacy stewardship expertise; D misassigns the core prescribing-review authority.

independent_second_pass: Fresh adversarial pass rechecked CDC currentness, the separation of Accountability, Pharmacy Expertise, and Action elements, each distractor, unsupported-precision risk, cueing, ambiguity, Management of Care blueprint fit, and entry-level relevance. No unresolved conflict remains after narrowing the correct-option wording.
